actCall.introStatic: Something in your week changed. Call the front desk, say what you need, and pick a time that fits your week.
actCall.introTail: Call the front desk, say what you need, and pick a time that fits your week.
actCall.goodFb: That’s what a good call sounds like.
actCall.callDone: Call done. Now try it with clearer lines.
actCall.stayed: You stayed on the call and kept going
actCall.jot: Jot down your plan before you call: who you are, why, and when you’re free.
actCall.ct: Here are the times I have: {t0}, {t1}, or {t2}.
hold: Okay, let me check the book. One moment.

calls.why: my team added a practice then
calls.intro: Your haircut clashes with a new practice.
calls.confirm: Fresh Cuts: Sam is booked Saturday at 10:00 with Marcus. See you then!

calls.why: my class has a field trip that day
calls.intro: Your dentist checkup lands on the day of a class field trip.
week: The field trip takes all of Friday.
calls.confirm: Bright Smiles Dental: Sam is booked Wednesday at 4:00 with Dr. Lee. Reply C to cancel.

calls.why: my cousin’s birthday party is that morning
calls.intro: Your swim lesson clashes with your cousin’s birthday party.
week: The party runs Saturday 9:00 to noon.
calls.confirm: Westside Rec Center: Sam is booked for a swim lesson Saturday at 1:00 with Coach Bea.

st.q: {who} picks up. What do you say?
st.n: Start with hello and your name.

r: Hi {me}! How can I help you?
Hello? Sorry, who is this?
~You tell {obj} you’re {me}.
Hi {me}. How can I help you?
c.tip: Say your name right away. It helps {who} find your visit.

c.t: Yeah, I need to change my {thing}.
r: Okay... who is this, so I can look you up?
~You tell {obj} you’re {me}.
Thanks, {me}. What’s going on?
c.tip: Start with hello and your name. It’s friendlier, and it helps {who} look you up.

st.n: Say why you’re calling in one clear sentence.

c.t: I have {thingA} {had}, but {why}. I need to move it.
r: Oh, got it. I see you {had}{P}.
What would you like to do?

c.t: Um, I have a thing. It’s about my appointment.
r: Okay... which appointment? What’s the thing?
~You explain it’s your {had} {thing} and {whyShort}.
Oh, I see you {had}{P}. What would you like to do?
c.tip: Say the day, the time and the problem in one sentence. Then {who} knows what you need.

c.t: Your schedule is messed up. Fix my appointment.
r: Oh! Sorry about that. Which appointment is it?
~You explain it’s your {had} {thing} and your own plans changed.
Okay, I see you {had}{P}. What would you like to do?
c.tip: Nothing is wrong with their schedule. Yours changed. Say that calmly and {who} will help.

st.s: Asked for a new time politely

c.t: Could I move it to {want}, please?
r: @hold
Change it to what? I need a day or a time.
~You say you want {want}.
@hold
c.tip: Tell {who} what you want: {want}. “Change it” can mean a lot of things.

c.t: Just give me a new time. I’m busy.
r: Okay, okay.
@hold
c.tip: Please makes a big difference. A kind voice gets help faster, even when you’re in a hurry.

st.q: {who} read out some times. Which one do you take?
st.s: Picked a time that fits your week
st.n: Check Your week before you pick a time.

r: {Good}. Perfect, that one’s open. I’ll put you down.
{Clash}, okay.
~Wait. Your week says {clashWhy}. You ask for {good} instead.
No problem. {Good} is open. I’ll put you down.
c.tip: {Clash} clashes with {clashWith}. Check Your week first. {goodFreeCap} is free.

r: Um, okay. {Good} is open, so I’ll put you down for that.
c.tip: Pick a time yourself. {who} can’t see your week, and a time that clashes would mean another call.

st.q: Say it back to be sure.
st.s: Repeated the day and time back
st.n: Repeat the day and time back before you hang up.

c.t: So that’s {good}, not {clashDay}. Is that right?
r: Yes, that’s right. {Good}, with {pro}.
Anything else I can help with?

c.t: Okay, cool. So it’s all set?
r: Yep, all set. That’s {good}.
Anything else I can help with?
c.tip: Say the day and time back yourself. It catches mix-ups, like {clashDay} instead of {goodDay}.

c.t: Fine. Just don’t mess it up this time.
r: Oh. I won’t. You’re down for {good}.
Anything else I can help with?
c.tip: Saying the day and time back is how you check. Blaming the desk makes the call feel tense.

st.q: Time to wrap up the call.

c.t: No, that’s all. Thank you, {who}! See you {goodDay}.
r: You’re welcome, {me}! See you {good}. Bye!
Okay. Bye now.
c.tip: A quick thank you ends the call on a good note.

r: ...Bye.
c.tip: Say thank you before you hang up. It only takes a second, and people remember it.
